decision: Replace RTDB latest-fix writes with one small Firestore latest-point document. Direct listeners use current Firestore authority; do not mirror every fix or maintain a second asynchronous authorization database.

dispatch.pointReads: Only displayed GPS-active jobs, maximum 200; no collection or RTDB tree scan

reads.legacyFallback: Only when no primary point exists, matching shipper and point time at/after current assignment and acceptance. Never fall back from an invalid existing primary.

security: Current enabled profile and matching staff claims; customer ownership remains identity-based
Canonical assignment checked within each write transaction and browser rule evaluation
Only exact-document gets; no browser writes or collection lists
No customer, address, payment or OTP in the location document
Reassignment and acceptance remove old primary points atomically

cost.qualification: Zero periodic calls requires the separately verified frontend event cutover. This backend alone does not remove polling and temporarily adds a marker and point read to old clients.
costsToInclude: accepted and rejected write transactions plus retries
location writes and TTL deletion write units
realtime update units and dependent security-rule reads
extra metadata markers on business changes
Function CPU, duration, network egress and actual document byte sizes
cost.reason: Do not equate fewer callables with guaranteed lower total cost; Enterprise byte units and listener fan-out must be measured.

prerequisites: CI and CodeQL on exact source
TTL ACTIVE on named database after empty-namespace check
Deploy tracking and dispatch readers before location writer
Deploy assignment/acceptance invalidation and the two existing order/delivery triggers
Verify exact serving revisions and named rules hash
Deploy writer last, then frontend event cutover
rollout.workflowNote: First release dispatched from earlier main must verify the new TTL prerequisite in release control as well; the embedded guard applies once this workflow is merged.
rollout.rollback: Roll back frontend event consumption and both readers together before reverting to the RTDB writer. Keeping a primary-preferring reader with an old RTDB-only writer can show a stale primary until expiry.

remaining: Tracking frontend event/GPS subscriptions and mobile tests
Measurement of total cost under representative viewer/shipper fan-out
